title: Urban Traffic Management Platform
shortDescription: A distributed microservices-based platform for managing and reporting urban traffic incidents in real time, featuring interactive map visualization, authentication, and containerized deployment.

details.overview: A distributed microservices-based platform designed for managing and reporting urban traffic incidents in real time. The system supports multiple user roles with different access levels and provides interactive map-based visualization of traffic events across a city.
details.problem: Urban traffic management requires real-time coordination between multiple stakeholders — incident reporters, administrators, and field responders. Existing solutions often lack real-time capabilities, proper role separation, or visual mapping of incidents.
details.solution: Built a microservices architecture with a GraphQL API gateway, JWT-based authentication with role-based access control, and an interactive map visualization layer using Leaflet. The system supports real-time incident reporting and an admin dashboard for monitoring.
details.architecture: The platform uses a microservices architecture with separate services for authentication, incident management, and user management. A GraphQL API gateway (Apollo Server) routes requests to the appropriate service. The frontend is built with Next.js/React, and PostgreSQL is used for persistent storage. Docker and GitHub Actions handle deployment and CI/CD.
details.challenges: Coordinating communication between microservices while maintaining data consistency, implementing secure JWT authentication with role-based access across service boundaries, and designing the real-time incident reporting pipeline.
details.whatILearned: Microservices architecture patterns, GraphQL API design with Apollo Server, real-time data handling with WebSockets, role-based access control implementation, and containerized deployment with Docker.

title: Big Data Analytics Pipeline
shortDescription: An end-to-end Big Data processing pipeline built for large-scale data ingestion, distributed processing, storage, and visualization.

details.overview: An end-to-end Big Data processing pipeline designed for large-scale data ingestion, distributed processing, storage, and visualization. The system handles the full data lifecycle from raw ingestion through transformation to business intelligence dashboards.
details.problem: Processing and analyzing large volumes of data requires distributed computing frameworks, proper storage strategies, and visualization tools that can handle scale without sacrificing performance or reliability.
details.solution: Built a complete pipeline using Apache Spark for distributed processing, Hadoop HDFS for scalable storage, PostgreSQL for structured data, Python for ETL orchestration, and Power BI for visualization. The entire stack is containerized with Docker.
details.architecture: The pipeline follows a standard ETL pattern: data is ingested into HDFS, processed with Spark jobs (Python), stored in PostgreSQL for querying, and visualized through Power BI dashboards. Docker containers ensure reproducibility across environments.
details.challenges: Designing efficient distributed processing pipelines, managing data flow between Hadoop HDFS and PostgreSQL, optimizing Spark jobs for performance, and creating meaningful visualizations from processed data.
details.whatILearned: Distributed computing with Apache Spark, Hadoop HDFS data storage patterns, ETL pipeline design, data warehousing concepts, and translating raw data into business intelligence.

title: TuniWay
shortDescription: A tourism exploration platform designed to simplify navigation and discovery across Tunisia through interactive and user-oriented features.

details.overview: A full-stack tourism exploration platform designed to simplify navigation and discovery across Tunisia. The application combines interactive maps, user authentication, a chat system, and an AI-powered chatbot to help travelers explore Tunisian destinations.
details.problem: Tourists visiting Tunisia often struggle to find reliable, curated information about local attractions, restaurants, and experiences. Existing travel apps may not provide localized content or interactive features for the Tunisian context.
details.solution: Built a full-stack application with Angular on the frontend, Spring Boot for the backend, and MongoDB for flexible data storage. The platform includes user authentication, a real-time chat system, an AI chatbot for recommendations, and interactive navigation features.
details.architecture: Angular handles the frontend UI with interactive components. Spring Boot provides RESTful APIs and business logic. MongoDB stores flexible document-based data for attractions, user profiles, and chat history. The architecture supports real-time features through WebSocket integration.
details.challenges: Implementing real-time chat functionality, integrating an AI chatbot for tourism recommendations, designing an intuitive navigation interface, and handling the flexible data requirements of tourism content.
details.whatILearned: Full-stack development with Angular and Spring Boot, NoSQL database design with MongoDB, real-time communication implementation, and AI integration for user-facing features.

title: TravelTun
shortDescription: A multi-platform tourism application for discovering local heritage and booking travel experiences with an integrated administration dashboard.

details.overview: A multi-platform tourism application for discovering local heritage and booking travel experiences. The app features a Flutter mobile client, a web-based admin dashboard, Firebase for backend services, and Flask for API management.
details.problem: Local tourism businesses in Tunisia need a digital platform to showcase their offerings, manage bookings, and interact with customers. Travelers need a reliable way to discover and book authentic local experiences.
details.solution: Built a cross-platform Flutter mobile app with a web admin interface. Firebase handles authentication, real-time database, and cloud storage. Flask provides the API layer for business logic. The system includes booking, reviews, payments, and real-time notifications.
details.architecture: Flutter provides the mobile UI with a single codebase for iOS and Android. Firebase services handle authentication, Firestore for the database, and Cloud Storage for media. Flask serves as the backend API for complex business logic. The admin dashboard is a separate web application.
details.challenges: Building a cross-platform mobile experience with Flutter, integrating multiple Firebase services, implementing a payment system, and designing an admin dashboard that provides meaningful management capabilities.
details.whatILearned: Cross-platform mobile development with Flutter, Firebase ecosystem integration, payment system implementation, and building admin interfaces for non-technical users.

title: School Management System
shortDescription: A backend-focused academic management system designed to manage students, teachers, scheduling, and school operations.

details.overview: A backend-focused academic management system designed to manage students, teachers, scheduling, and school operations. The system provides a CLI interface for administrative tasks and emphasizes data integrity and role-based access control.
details.problem: Schools need efficient systems to manage student records, teacher assignments, course scheduling, and grade tracking. Manual processes are error-prone and time-consuming for administrators.
details.solution: Built a Python backend with PostgreSQL for data storage and a CLI interface for administrative operations. The system supports role-based access, grade tracking, attendance management, automatic timetable generation, and report generation.
details.architecture: Python handles business logic and data access through a structured CLI interface. PostgreSQL provides reliable relational data storage with proper constraints and relationships. The system is designed around role-based access control to ensure data security.
details.challenges: Designing a robust database schema for school operations, implementing automatic timetable generation with constraint satisfaction, and ensuring data integrity across complex relationships.
details.whatILearned: Database design for complex relational data, CLI application architecture, role-based access control patterns, and constraint-based scheduling algorithms.

title: MedFlow — Healthcare SaaS Platform
shortDescription: A full-stack healthcare SaaS platform that digitizes the clinical workflow — from appointment booking through e-prescriptions and QR-verified pharmacy fulfillment, with role-based access and real-time doctor-patient messaging.
features: Role-based Access Control (RBAC) for admins, doctors, patients, secretaries, and pharmacists
JWT + OAuth2 Authentication with Argon2 password hashing
Electronic Prescriptions with QR code generation, line items, lab tests, and versioned fulfillment tracking
Pharmacy Module with inventory batches, stock movements, QR verification, and concurrency-safe dispensing
Appointment Scheduling with doctor availability and status history
Modular Monolith Architecture with clean domain boundaries
SpringDoc OpenAPI / Swagger UI and REST Docs

details.role: Owned the prescription and localization areas of the MedFlow MVP. Implemented QR-verified pharmacy workflows and contributed to the real-time messaging system.
details.overview: A full-stack healthcare SaaS platform that digitizes the clinical workflow — from appointment booking through e-prescriptions and QR-verified pharmacy fulfillment, with role-based access and real-time doctor-patient messaging.
details.problem: Healthcare workflows are often fragmented across paper-based systems, disconnected software tools, and manual processes. This leads to inefficiencies in prescription management, pharmacy fulfillment, appointment scheduling, and patient-doctor communication.
details.solution: Built a modular monolith with Spring Boot 4.1 on the backend and React 19 on the frontend. The system provides electronic prescriptions with QR verification, a pharmacy module with inventory management, appointment scheduling, real-time chat, and role-based access for five distinct user roles.
details.architecture: Modular monolith architecture with clean domain boundaries using Spring Boot 4.1. Backend uses Spring Security with OAuth2/JWT and Argon2 password hashing. Database migrations managed with Liquibase. Frontend built with React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8, TailwindCSS 4, and shadcn/ui. Real-time features via WebSocket/STOMP. Docker Compose for development. GitLab CI/CD for deployment.
details.challenges: Designing a modular monolith with clean domain boundaries, implementing QR-verified prescription and pharmacy workflows, managing concurrent pharmacy dispensing operations, building a real-time chat system, and integrating transactional notification events.
details.whatILearned: Modular monolith architecture patterns, Spring Boot 4.1 with modern Spring ecosystem, healthcare domain modeling, QR code generation and verification workflows, and concurrent operation handling in a multi-role system.

title: AI Knowledge & HR Copilot
shortDescription: An internal AI assistant combining a RAG knowledge base with HR workflows — vector-search document retrieval with a two-layer hallucination-refusal system, plus CV extraction and candidate scoring.
features: RAG-based Knowledge Base with document chunking and embedding pipeline
HNSW-indexed Vector Search with cosine similarity
Two-layer Hallucination-refusal System (threshold gate + context-grounded generation)
CV Extraction via Gemini JSON-schema mode
Candidate Scoring with deterministic skill-matching algorithm (0-100)
Onboarding Checklists grounded in company documents
Jest Unit Tests + E2E Tests Against Live Database

details.role: Built the AI Knowledge & HR Copilot as the primary backend engineer — the RAG pipeline, vector search, hallucination prevention, CV extraction, and HR workflow features.
details.overview: An internal AI assistant combining a RAG-based knowledge base with structured HR workflows. The system provides vector-search document retrieval with a two-layer hallucination-refusal system, CV extraction, and candidate scoring.
details.problem: Organizations need efficient ways to search internal documents, onboard new employees, and evaluate candidates. Traditional keyword search misses semantic context, and HR processes are often manual and time-consuming.
details.solution: Built a pnpm monorepo with NestJS 11 backend and Next.js 16 frontend. Implemented a RAG pipeline with document chunking, embedding generation, and HNSW-indexed vector search using pgvector. Added a two-layer hallucination-refusal system for reliable AI-generated answers. CV extraction uses Gemini's JSON-schema mode with deterministic candidate scoring.
details.architecture: pnpm monorepo with NestJS 11 (backend) and Next.js 16 (frontend). PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector for vector storage and HNSW indexing. Document chunking and embedding pipeline for RAG. Two-layer hallucination-refusal: threshold gate + context-grounded generation. JWT/Passport authentication with RBAC. Docker for development. GitLab CI for deployment.
details.challenges: Implementing reliable RAG with hallucination prevention, designing the two-layer refusal system, building a robust document chunking and embedding pipeline, and creating deterministic candidate scoring that integrates with AI-extracted CV data.
details.whatILearned: RAG architecture patterns, vector database design with pgvector, hallucination prevention strategies, Gemini API integration for structured extraction, and monorepo management with pnpm workspaces.
